release_notes:
New app: 911 Scripting Prep

What it does: it builds the SSPO scripting sheet out of an award review
somebody has already checked, instead of it being typed out line by line.

  - It reads the review's Working Forecast Input sheet - one line per nest -
    and looks each source material up in the Working Forecast List to get its
    designation and its size.

  - It works off a read-only copy of the forecast, so the live file is never
    opened.

  - Columns that need a person - PO NO, LINE, PROMISE DATE, part rev, clauses,
    ship-to - get their heading and stay blank. PART REV, STANDARD CLAUSES,
    SHIP, QTY and UNIT PRICE can be set once in the app's settings when they
    are the same across a whole award.

  - It never guesses a material. Anything it cannot find in the forecast is
    left blank and listed for you, not filled in with something close.

What you get at the end: one workbook saved next to the award review, with a
PO Data sheet and a Part Data sheet. Everything the app worked out is in red,
so you can see at a glance what came from it and what is still yours to fill
in. If anything did not resolve there is a third sheet called Unresolved,
naming the nests that need their material and size typed in - delete that
sheet once they are in. It is not created at all when everything resolves.

How to run it: run 911 SSPO Award Review on the award package first, then run
this and pick the award review workbook that one wrote. Your Forecast and
Inventory Reports folder needs to be synced, not cloud only.

Fixes

  - 911 PO PDF Extractor is back. It got replaced by Scripting Prep, which
    was wrong - the two do opposite jobs. The extractor reads an incoming PO
    packet from EB; Scripting Prep builds the outgoing scripting sheet. Both
    are here now, and an update will not remove it again. One thing to do:
    that earlier change took the extractor's tile off your Home screen, so
    add it back from the Library once. It stays after that.

  - A dead tile left behind by the same renaming clears itself the next time
    you start TechDeck.

  - 911 Inspection Dimensions starts with no nests ticked, the same as 911
    Setup. You tick the ones you want, instead of unticking the ones you
    don't.
